subject: chemistry

moments.title: EPA's green chemistry programme
moments.body: Anastas coins 'green chemistry' at the US EPA. The aim: chemical processes that reduce or eliminate hazardous substances.
moments.takeaway: Chemistry takes responsibility for its environmental footprint.

moments.title: Twelve Principles
moments.body: Their book 'Green Chemistry: Theory and Practice' sets out 12 principles: atom economy, less hazardous synthesis, renewable feedstocks, etc. The principles become standard teaching.

moments.title: Olefin metathesis Nobel
moments.body: Catalysts for olefin metathesis enable green synthesis routes with high atom economy. The 2005 Nobel explicitly cites the contribution to green chemistry.
moments.takeaway: Catalysis becomes the engine of green chemistry.

moments.title: Circular chemistry
moments.body: Chemical recycling of plastics, CO2 utilisation, electrochemical synthesis with renewable electricity, and bio-based feedstocks are major research areas. The 12 principles guide design.
moments.takeaway: Chemistry is being reinvented to fit within planetary limits.

now.title: Where we are today
now.body: Green chemistry is now a standard MSc/PhD topic. Industry routinely uses E-factor (waste/product) as a metric. Green pharma is a multi-billion-dollar industry.
now.open_questions: Can chemistry's emissions reach net-zero by 2050? Can plastics be made fully circular?

reflection: Chemistry created the pollution problems and now is being asked to solve them. Can the same discipline that caused the harm cure it?
